And if Reza has indeed truly embraced Islam sincerely because of Allah, not because of other reasons, Father can only pray for the best.” He looked at Reza. “But remember, Reza. Becoming a Muslim means you must also be ready to carry responsibility, especially if you intend to marry Father's daughter. The responsibility to guide her, protect her, and bring her closer to Allah.” “I understand, Pak. And I will try with all my strength to become a good husband and imam for Nisa, if you both bless us,” said Reza, there was a tremor of emotion in his voice.

Although there was no explicit “yes” yet for a marriage, Nisa and Reza felt this meeting was far more positive than before. There was a glimmer of hope that the bridge was beginning to be built, though maybe still fragile.

Before Reza took his leave, Fatima invited Nisa to speak briefly in the kitchen, while Reza waited in the living room with Ahmed, whose attitude was now slightly more fluid and had even started asking about Reza's family background. “Nis,” said Fatima while holding her daughter's hand. “Mother sees, you're happier now. And Reza… he looks different. Calmer.” Nisa nodded, her tears again pooling. “Yes, Ma, he's changed a lot.” “Take good care of yourself, dear. Guard your faith, guard Reza's faith too. Remind each other in goodness,” Fatima advised. “And… if you two are indeed serious, discuss the next step properly. Don't do things that could make Allah angry before their time.”

Thump. Nisa's heart felt like it stopped beating hearing her mother's last sentence. Did her mother know something? Was there a suspicious tone in her words? Nisa looked at her mother, trying to read her expression, but Fatima's face looked calm and full of affection as usual. Maybe that was just a mother's general advice to her daughter. Nisa tried to dismiss her unease. “God willing, Bu. Thank you for the prayers,” Nisa answered, trying to smile.

While walking home with Reza, Nisa told about her conversation with her mother. Reza also told how Ahmed had started asking more about his family and his future plans, no longer just about his religion. “Seems like, they're starting to open their hearts, right, Rez?” said Nisa full of hope. Reza smiled, gripping Nisa's hand. “Alhamdulillah. This is all thanks to our patience and prayers, Nis. And of course, because of your courage to keep fighting for us.” “We fought, Rez. Not just me,” Nisa corrected.

They knew, this was just the first step. There was still much they had to prove, especially Reza. He had to be able to show his consistency as a Muslim, and also as a responsible prospective son-in-law.

That night, as Nisa walked Reza to the front of her house's street, there was a feeling of relief and optimism greater than before. That bridge might not yet be fully sturdy, but its foundation was starting to be visible. And they both were determined to keep building it, stone by stone, with love, faith, patience, and prayer. Their “Faith and Beats” journey entered a new chapter, where harmony between two worlds now felt increasingly possible to achieve.
15: The month following Reza's decision to embrace Islam and their effort to build a bridge with Nisa's family was a period full of busyness, planning, and also learning. The formal proposal from Reza to Nisa's family, though initially colored by slight residual tension from the previous conflict, was finally received with more open hearts by Ahmed and Fatima. They saw earnestness in Reza's eyes, the positive change within him, and most importantly, the happiness that couldn't be hidden from their daughter Nisa's face.

Planning the wedding became its own adventure for Nisa and Reza. They both wanted a celebration that not only united their love, but also honored two worlds now blending: the Islamic faith they held together, Nisa's family's thick tradition, the modern touch from Reza's background, and of course, their love for music.

“So, for the marriage contract, we'll use complete Sundanese custom according to your Mama and Papa's wish, right, Nis?” Reza asked one afternoon while they sat at a cafe, surrounded by piles of wedding vendor brochures and small notes. He was now fluent in using “Mama” and “Papa” to refer to Nisa's parents. Nisa smiled, her heart warming. “Yes, Rez. Mama will surely be so happy. She's long dreamed of me wearing the Sundanese siger and brocade kebaya on my wedding day.” “I also can't wait to see you wear it,” Reza said sincerely, his eyes looking at Nisa with full love. “You'll surely be so beautiful. But, can I request something for the reception?” “Of course, Rez. This is our wedding, both of ours,” Nisa answered gently.

Reza took out his tablet, showing some more modern reception decoration concepts, with a touch of artistic lighting and stage arrangement reminiscent of a music festival atmosphere, but still elegant. “How about we make the reception more… us? There's a traditional touch, but there's also an area where we can enjoy the music we love?” Nisa laughed. “You mean, there'll be a DJ Rez G booth at our own wedding?” Reza grinned. “Why not? Or at least, we can play our chosen EDM playlist after all the formal processions are done. Music is part of our story, Nis.”

Discussions like this colored their wedding preparations. There was bargaining, there was compromise, but always ended with understanding and smiles. Nisa's family, especially her mother, was initially a bit worried the reception would be too “Westernized.” However, Nisa and Reza patiently explained they wanted to honor all parties. There would be an area for senior guests with gentler music and traditional dishes, but there would also be space for their friends to celebrate in a more modern way.

The wedding dress fitting process became an emotional moment for Nisa. When she tried on the ivory-white brocade kebaya with glittering sequin details, paired with a magnificent Sundanese siger, tears of emotion couldn't be held back from Fatima's eyes. “Mother's child is all grown up,” she whispered while hugging Nisa. Ahmed, who also accompanied them, looked teary-eyed even though he tried to hide it behind his firm attitude. Reza, who wore a matching-colored beskap, looked so dashing and different from his everyday casual appearance. He looked at Nisa with full admiration. “You're truly like a princess, Nis,” he praised sincerely.

Amid the busyness of wedding preparation, Nisa and Reza didn't forget the spiritual aspect. They became increasingly diligent in worshipping together, deepening their religious understanding, and praying that everything would be made smooth. The burden of the secret from that forbidden night, though still there, now felt a little lighter. This marriage, for them, wasn't just the union of two souls, but also a big step to sanctify their relationship in Allah's eyes, a real form of their repentance and commitment to build a household blessed by Him.

Midodareni night, the night before the marriage contract, Nisa's house was filled with relatives. An atmosphere of emotion and sacredness was so palpable. Nisa, who was secluded in her room, received final advice from her mother and family elders. She felt so loved and blessed. Reza, according to custom, wasn't permitted to meet Nisa that night. He spent his night praying and reflecting, preparing himself to speak the ijab kabul the next day. There was extraordinary nervousness, but also deep peace in his heart. He felt ready to become Nisa's husband, to become the imam for his family later.

And finally, that long-awaited day arrived — October 30, a date that from that day on they would always celebrate every year as their anniversary. Jakarta's sky that morning was clear, as clear as Nisa's and Reza's hearts. The marriage contract procession was held at a beautiful grand mosque, not far from Nisa's house. White and soft-green flower decorations adorned every corner of the mosque, creating an atmosphere so solemn and calming.

Nisa, wrapped in an ivory-white kebaya and glittering Sundanese siger, walked slowly toward the contract table, accompanied by both her parents. Her heart pounded hard, but the smile never left her lips. Her eyes met Reza's gaze, who was already seated before the marriage officiant and the witnesses. Reza, with a white beskap and matching peci, looked so calm and dignified. His blue eyes, which usually radiated a DJ's characteristic wild energy, now radiated gentleness, love, and deep earnestness.

Ustaz Rahman, who was also present as one of the witnesses, gave a marriage sermon so touching, speaking about the meaning of marriage in Islam, about husband and wife's responsibilities, and about the importance of building a household on a foundation of piety and compassion. Nisa and Reza listened with full attention, absorbing every word of advice.

When the time came for the ijab kabul, the atmosphere became so silent. Ahmed, Nisa's father, shook Reza's hand tightly. There was a tremor of emotion in his voice as he spoke the ijab sentence, handing over his daughter to be married by Reza. “Son Reza Satria bin Michael John, I marry and wed you to my biological daughter, Nisa Farha binti Ahmed Suryadi, with a dowry of a set of prayer equipment and 201 grams of gold paid in cash.”

All eyes turned to Reza. He took a deep breath, looked at Ahmed firmly, then with a clear and resounding voice, he spoke the kabul sentence: “I accept the marriage and wedding of Nisa Farha binti Ahmed Suryadi with the mentioned dowry, paid in cash.”

“Valid?” the officiant asked the witnesses. “VALID!” the witnesses answered in unison, followed by a thunderous “Alhamdulillah” from all those present. Nisa's tears could no longer be held back. This time not tears of sadness or doubt, but tears of pure happiness. Reza was now her husband. They had legally become husband and wife in the eyes of religion and state. The burden of the secret they'd carried all this time seemed lifted, replaced by a feeling of relief and new sanctity.

Reza turned toward Nisa, a smile carved on his face. He extended his hand, and Nisa welcomed it. They looked at each other, conveying all the love, gratitude, and unspoken promises. After the closing prayer and the signing of the marriage book, Reza handed over the dowry to Nisa, then gently kissed his wife's forehead for the first time as a lawful couple. A kiss full of love, respect, and commitment.

The wedding reception was held that night at a multipurpose hall that had been transformed into something so beautiful. In accordance with Nisa's and Reza's wishes, there was a blend of traditional and modern elements. A classic Sundanese-style wedding dais became the center of attention, but on the other side of the room, there was a small stage with more dynamic lighting, the place where later there would be more contemporary music entertainment.

Nisa and Reza, now wrapped in matching reception attire — Nisa with an elegant champagne-colored modern Muslimah gown, and Reza with a matching-colored suit — welcomed the guests with happy smiles. Nisa's extended family, who once doubted, now looked friendlier and accepting. Some aunts and cousins even openly praised Reza's handsomeness and politeness. Reza's family, who also attended from abroad, looked so enthusiastic and enchanted by the beauty of Indonesian wedding tradition. Reza's mother, Rose, ceaselessly hugged Nisa and expressed her happiness.

After the group photo session and enjoying the dishes, the entertainment program began. Initially filled with acoustic music performances presenting romantic songs and some regional songs. However, after the formal program and the session for senior guests finished, the atmosphere began to change. The lights began being played more dynamically, and from the speakers began sounding a more upbeat electronic music intro.

This was a surprise Reza had prepared. It wasn't he himself who performed as DJ, because he wanted to enjoy this moment fully as the groom. But he had invited one of his DJ friends who was also quite well known, to play a special set they'd discussed together: a blend of classic EDM songs evoking nostalgia, some of Nisa's favorite melodic house songs, and even some of Reza's new tracks with a more positive and uplifting nuance.

Initially, some guests from Nisa's family side looked a bit surprised. However, seeing Nisa and Reza so enjoying that music, dancing freely but still politely, and seeing many of their young friends joining to liven up the dance floor, the atmosphere became more fluid. Even Ahmed and Fatima were seen smiling, though maybe still a bit awkward. They saw the happiness so real on their daughter's face, and that was enough for them.

Yusuf and Salma also attended, joining to celebrate their friends' happiness. “I never expected to see you this happy, Nis,” said Salma while hugging Nisa. “And Reza, you're truly an extraordinary man.” “All this is also thanks to your support,” Reza said sincerely.

That night became a true celebration of love. A celebration of two souls who had found each other, passed through various obstacles, and finally united in the sacred bond of marriage. Their “Faith and Beats” symphony reached a beautiful crescendo, where faith and melody no longer conflicted, but blended harmoniously creating a new melody of life full of hope.

As the night grew later and the guests began gradually going home, Nisa and Reza stood together in a corner of the room, gazing at their wedding dais still magnificent. Reza's hand circled Nisa's waist, pulling her closer. “Tired?” Reza asked gently. Nisa rested her head on Reza's shoulder. “A little. But so happy.” “Me too,” said Reza. “This is the best day of my life.” He looked deep into Nisa's eyes. “Thank you for being willing to fight alongside me, Nisa Farha, my Wife.” Nisa smiled, her heart overflowing. “Thank you too for choosing me, Reza Satria, my Husband.”

They knew, this marriage wasn't the end of their journey, but the beginning of a new chapter that would be full of learning, challenges, and of course, love. But that night, amid the remnants of their wedding party's festivity, there was only gratitude and boundless happiness. Two worlds had united, two hearts had blended, in an eternal symphony blessed by the Creator.
16: Five months had passed since the day that changed everything for Reza Satria: his marriage to Nisa. Six months since he spoke the two shahada sentences, witnessed by Nisa, Yusuf, and Ustaz Rahman. Six months that felt like an emotional and spiritual roller coaster journey, full of learning, adjustment, and also boundless happiness. New life as a Muslim, and as Nisa's husband who was now slowly beginning to be accepted by her family, had brought big change within Reza.

That change wasn't only visible from his increasingly consistent worship routine — the five daily prayers he no longer abandoned, his Monday and Thursday fasting that began becoming habit, and his increasingly fluent ability to read the Qur'an thanks to patient guidance from Nisa, his wife, and also Ustaz Rahman. That change also radiated from his aura. Reza who once sometimes looked restless and searching, now appeared calmer, more peaceful, and more focused. There was a kind of new light in his eyes, the light of sincere faith.

However, integrating his new identity as a Muslim with his established life as DJ Rez G, an EDM music maestro, wasn't an easy matter. This was the biggest challenge he had to face daily. The electronic music world, with all its glitter and freedom, often intersected with things he now understood contradicted Islamic values.

“How is it, Rez? Ready to drop beats that'll blow up the dance floor tonight?” asked Jason, his manager, one afternoon at Reza's studio. They were discussing the set list for Reza's performance at one of the big music festivals that weekend. Reza smiled thinly. “Ready, Jas. But there are some tracks I want to revise a bit. Maybe some of the lyrics are too… vulgar, or the message doesn't fit.” Jason raised one eyebrow. “Revise? Since when did you become a 'music censor' like this, Rez? Aren't you usually the most anti-censorship?” Reza laughed a little. “Not censorship, Jas. More like… adjustment. I want my music to not just make people move, but also be able to give positive energy, or at least not bring bad influence.”

This was one concrete change Reza began applying. He became more selective in choosing songs he played or produced. He began avoiding songs with lyrics too explicit, that glorified hedonism, or that had negative messages. He even began experimenting by inserting ethnic elements or more calming and meaning-laden melodies into his music, creating a unique blend between modern EDM pounding and a more reflective touch. Some other music producers or fellow DJs might consider it strange, but Reza didn't care. He felt this was part of his new journey, part of his effort to align “faith” and “beats” in his life.

Nisa was his biggest supporter in this process. She often accompanied Reza at the studio, listening to his new song demos, and giving input from her perspective as a Muslimah and also a heavy EDM lover. “This one is so cool, Rez!” Nisa exclaimed one day, after Reza played a new progressive house track that had a very touching melodic arrangement, blended with a rhythm that stayed energetic but felt more “deep.” “It feels… goosebump-inducing. There's a different nuance, more soulful, but still fun to listen to.” Reza smiled with relief. “Thank God you like it. I was a bit worried this would sound strange or actually become less EDM.” “Not at all,” Nisa said sincerely. “This is so creative. You succeeded in bringing something new and fresh to your music, something reflecting who you are now.”

Nisa's love for EDM music now felt freer and more whole. Before, she always hid it, enjoyed it with guilt. Now, with Reza at her side, a Muslim who was also a DJ, she felt she could be herself. Her inner conflict that once so tortured her, now slowly subsided, replaced by gratitude and peace. She was no longer afraid of being judged. She even began daring to share this passion with some of her other close friends, like Salma, who turned out could also enjoy some lighter EDM songs after Nisa introduced her.

They both often spent time together, not only to study religion or discuss music, but also doing simple things like other couples. Going for dinner at Nisa's favorite satay stall, watching a movie at the cinema, or just an afternoon walk in the city park while enjoying ice cream. However, in every togetherness, there was always a spiritual touch coloring it. They would pause briefly to pray Maghrib at the nearest prayer room if they were out, or remind each other to read a prayer before eating. Small things that made their relationship feel increasingly blessed.

Reza's relationship with Nisa's family also showed significant progress, though moving slowly and full of caution. Ahmed, Nisa's father, though still often showing a formal and slightly rigid attitude toward Reza, now began more often inviting him to talk, especially about Reza's development in studying Islam. He even several times tested Reza's memorization of short chapters or his knowledge of basic fiqh. Reza always answered patiently and humbly, admitting if there was something he didn't yet know and promising to study it further.

Fatima, Nisa's mother, seemed to soften faster. She saw the positive change in her daughter who now looked happier and calmer. She also saw Reza's earnestness in worship and his effort to adapt to their family's tradition. Fatima began often inviting Reza to join small family events, like dinner together or family gatherings even though there were still some relatives who looked at Reza with suspicious stares or whispered.

“Be patient, okay, Rez,” Nisa whispered once, when they were attending one of her cousins' thanksgiving events and she saw some less pleasant stares directed at Reza. “Not everyone can immediately accept. But slowly, they'll surely see your sincerity.” Reza smiled, gripping Nisa's hand under the table. “I'm fine, Nis. As long as you're by my side, I'm strong.”

Reza's biggest challenge as a Muslim DJ came when he had to perform at big events lasting until late at night, sometimes coinciding with prayer times, or in environments full of alcohol and free association. This was an inner struggle he continuously faced.

“Jas, I ask for help, if possible don't let my performance schedule crash with Maghrib or Isha prayer times. Or at least, give me a few minutes' break to pray backstage,” Reza asked his manager one day. Jason, who was initially confused by Reza's new requests, now began to understand a little. “Okay, Rez. I'll try. But you know, in this industry, flexibility is sometimes hard. Especially if you're the headliner.” “I know, Jas. But this is important to me,” Reza said firmly.

He also began being braver about refusing offers to perform at places he felt were too “dark” or not aligned with his new principles. Some promoters might be disappointed, some DJ colleagues might scoff, but Reza held firm to his decision. He remembered Yusuf's words that music itself isn't forbidden, but the environment and impact it causes need to be considered.

One night, after performing at a fairly big music festival, Reza felt very tired. He managed to get a break to pray Isha in a small room behind the stage, though he had to argue a bit with the committee. As he was tidying his equipment, a famous international DJ who also performed at that event approached him. “Hey, Rez G! Great set, man! I really liked your transition earlier, and there were some new tracks you played, they sounded so fresh!” that DJ praised. “Oh, thanks, man! Means a lot coming from you,” Reza answered, a bit surprised and also happy to receive praise from one of his idols. “But I noticed, you seem a bit different now?” that DJ continued. “Before you seemed more… wild on stage. Now calmer, but still powerful. And earlier I saw you seemed to be… praying backstage?” Reza smiled. “Yes, Bro. I'm trying to find a new balance in my life. Between music and… something more personal.” That DJ nodded, seeming to understand. “I understand what you mean. This industry can sometimes 'swallow' us alive if we don't have an anchor. Good for you, man, for finding yours.”
That brief conversation gave Reza new strength. It turned out, not everyone would scoff or not understand. There were also those who could appreciate his journey.

Nisa, on the other side, also experienced extraordinary personal growth. With Reza's support, she became more confident in expressing her love for EDM music. She no longer felt the need to hide it with excessive guilt. She began seeing that music, like other art forms, could be enjoyed and appreciated without having to violate her religion's boundaries, as long as she could guard herself and her intention.

She even began daring to write reviews about EDM albums or her favorite DJ sets on an anonymous personal blog. Writing became her way to channel her passion and knowledge about electronic music. She also began being more active discussing with Reza about technical aspects in music production, even occasionally giving melody or arrangement ideas for Reza's songs.

“You have talent to be a producer too, you know, Nis,” Reza said one day, after Nisa gave brilliant input about how to develop a melody loop into a whole song. Nisa laughed. “Ah, really? I'm just a listener.” “A listener with golden ears,” Reza retorted. “Seriously, sometime let's try making a track together in the studio. Faith and Beats project, how about it?” Nisa's eyes gleamed. That idea sounded very interesting. A music project that truly reflected the blend of their two worlds.

“Your tajwid recitation has gotten so much better, you know, Rez,” Nisa praised one night, after they finished praying Isha in congregation in Nisa's house's living room. Ahmed and Fatima, who happened to also pray together with them, smiled thinly hearing that praise. Reza blushed. “Still a lot to learn, Nis. The letter articulation points still often go wrong.” “It's fine, what matters is you keep trying,” said Ahmed, chiming in. This was one rare moment where her father showed a bit of warmth toward Reza. Nisa's heart warmed.

Slowly but surely, Nisa's family began seeing Reza's earnestness. They saw how Reza tried hard to become a good Muslim, how he respected their family's tradition, and most importantly, how he made Nisa happy. Although the journey to get full blessing was still long, at least that door had begun to open.

One weekend, Reza invited Nisa to a shady city park. Not to discuss music or religion, but just to relax and enjoy the afternoon. They sat under a big tree, watching children playing, and people passing by. “Nis,” Reza said slowly, breaking the comfortable silence between them. “I know, this journey of ours isn't easy. So many challenges, so much adjustment we have to make, especially me.” Nisa turned, looking into Reza's calm eyes. “But I want you to know,” Reza continued, his voice sincere. “Every second I pass in this journey, every difficulty I face, all of it feels worth it because you're by my side. You're the reason why I want to be better, Nis. You're… the greatest blessing in my life.” Tears of emotion again pooled at the corners of Nisa's eyes. She reached for Reza's hand, gripping it tightly. “You're also a blessing for me, Rez. You taught me many things about courage, about sincerity, and about how love and faith can walk side by side.”

They smiled at each other. Amid Jakarta city's hustle and bustle, under the shelter of that shady tree, two souls once separated by difference, now found harmony in the same faith and melody. Their new life might not always be easy, but they knew, as long as they had each other and held firm to their conviction, they would be able to face whatever storm came. Their “Faith and Beats” symphony still kept continuing, with new melodies increasingly beautiful and full of meaning, ready to be played on the real stage of life.
17: Five years had passed since Nisa and Reza Satria's blessed wedding day. Five years woven from strands of laughter, tears of emotion, ceaseless learning, and of course, love growing ever more deeply rooted. Their apartment in one corner of South Jakarta was now not just a place to live, but a small warm palace.

Their married life was a unique symphony. Nisa, now a more confident career woman and also a loving wife, had found the balance she once so longed for. Her love for EDM music was no longer a burdening secret. With Reza, she could enjoy every music genre freely, even often becoming the first critic for every new song demo Reza created. She was also active in social activities at the mosque near their home, finding happiness in sharing and helping others. Her figure once often shrouded in doubt and fear, now radiated an aura of calm and certainty.

Reza Satria, DJ Rez G, had also gone through an extraordinary transformation. His status as a convert was no longer just a label, but had become ingrained in every aspect of his life. He not only diligently carried out obligatory worship, but also kept deepening his religious understanding. His discussions with Ustaz Rahman or Yusuf he still often did, but now with deeper, more philosophical questions. He found that Islam wasn't only about ritual, but about a comprehensive outlook on life, which gave him peace and purpose.

His career as a DJ also evolved. He indeed didn't fully leave the big stages, but he became far more selective. He more often performed at events that had positive messages, music festivals with more diverse genres, or even charity events. His music itself experienced significant change. The bass pounding that once might have felt “dark” and wild, now more often blended with melodies inspired by nature's beauty, local wisdom, or even spiritual touches. The “Faith and Beats” project that once was only an idea, had now become his trademark. Some of his songs combining electronic music elements with poetic lyrics about universal love, peace, and gratitude, turned out to receive extraordinary reception, not only from the Muslim community, but also from electronic music listeners in general who longed for something more than just noise.

“Who would've thought, Ustaz Rahman's sermon about the beauty of Asmaul Husna could become inspiration for a trance song's breakdown, right?” Reza said with a laugh one afternoon, when he and Nisa were relaxing on their apartment balcony, enjoying warm ginger tea Nisa had made. Nisa smiled. “I already told you, inspiration can come from anywhere, Rez. What matters is the intention and how it's delivered.” “True, Darling. You're indeed my best teacher, in many things,” Reza gripped Nisa's hand, kissing it gently.

Their relationship with Nisa's family had now reached a point of harmony that once felt impossible. Ahmed and Fatima had fully accepted Reza as their son-in-law, even often boasting about Reza's earnestness in studying religion and how he brought positive influence for Nisa. They saw how this marriage had made their daughter increasingly mature, happy, and also increasingly devout. Not rarely, Ahmed invited Reza to pray Friday prayers together, or discussed religious issues warmly. Fatima now often asked Reza to taste her new cooking, or just share stories about daily activities. Their marriage became proof that after the darkness of mistake, there is always the light of forgiveness for those who sincerely return.

One day, Nisa gave Reza a surprise. Two airplane tickets and a travel brochure. “What's this, Nis?” Reza asked curiously. “A gift for our fifth wedding anniversary, and also realizing one of your old dreams,” Nisa said with a smile. Reza opened that brochure. His eyes widened. “Morocco? We're going to Morocco?” Nisa nodded enthusiastically. “Yes! We'll explore the beauty of Fes, Marrakech, see the Sahara Desert, and of course, seek new musical inspiration there!” Reza couldn't speak. He hugged Nisa tightly. “You're the most extraordinary woman I've ever known,” he whispered with emotion.

Several weeks later, Nisa and Reza truly began their adventure. In every city they visited, in every historical mosque they entered, in every busy traditional market, they felt Allah's greatness and the richness of Islamic civilization. Reza, with his camera, ceaselessly captured every moment, while Nisa noted every inspiration she received.

In Cordoba, they were enchanted by the majesty of the Mezquita Mosque-Cathedral. In Granada, they were swept away in the poetic beauty of the Alhambra. In Fes, Morocco, they got lost in the labyrinth of its old medina full of color and spice aroma. And finally, amid the magical silence of the Sahara Desert, under a spread of night sky studded with billions of stars, they again felt extraordinary closeness, both with the Creator and with each other.

Their trip to Morocco became one of the most memorable experiences in their lives. They were enchanted by the beauty of magnificent Islamic architecture, the friendliness of local residents, the richness of culture, and of course, the traditional Moroccan music so exotic. Reza recorded many sound samples, from the mystical strains of Gnawa music to the melodious call to prayer from ancient mosque minarets. Nisa herself felt like finding a new piece of her Islamic identity, seeing how Islam could blend so beautifully with rich local culture.

They sat atop a sand dune, just the two of them, accompanied by the warmth of a small campfire. “Before, I never dared to dream this far, Rez,” Nisa said softly, her voice carried by the gentle desert wind. “My life before felt so narrow, full of fear and doubt.” Reza wrapped his arm around Nisa's shoulder. “But you were brave, Nis. You dared to fight for what you believed, you dared to take risks. And look at us now.” “This is all also because of you, Rez,” Nisa replied. “You came bringing light, bringing courage. You helped me find myself, reconcile my faith with my passion.” “We complete each other, Darling,” Reza said. “You're my faith, I'm your beat. And together, we create the most beautiful symphony.”

They remembered again the long journey they'd been through. From the unexpected meeting at The Corrs concert, the discovery of a shared passion for EDM, Nisa's inner conflict, family rejection, Reza's spiritual journey, until the gift of this marriage became the turning point of their awareness. All of it was part of Allah's destiny that had shaped them into stronger, wiser, and more grateful individuals.

Amid the spread of Sahara Desert sand, as the setting sun created a stunning golden silhouette, Nisa and Reza sat together, reflecting. “Before, I never imagined my life would be like this, Rez,” Nisa said slowly, resting her head on Reza's shoulder. “Full of surprises, full of learning, and full of love.” Reza smiled, stroking Nisa's hair covered by her hijab. “Me too, Nis. Before my life felt… flat. There was only music and stage. But you came, bringing new color, bringing new meaning. And Islam… Islam gave me the direction I'd been searching for all this time.” He continued, “Sometimes I still can't believe, how a DJ like me could find peace in a religion that once felt so foreign. But that's guidance, right? Coming in an unexpected way, through an unexpected person.”

“And our music?” Nisa asked. “Do you still feel there's conflict between 'Faith' and 'Beats' within you?” Reza shook his head slowly. “Not anymore, Darling. I realize, both can walk side by side, even strengthen each other. My faith gives me inspiration to create more meaningful music, music that can touch the soul, not just raise adrenaline. And my music becomes my way to share the beauty and peace I found in my faith.” He looked deep into Nisa's eyes. “Just like you. You're the 'Faith' in my life, who always reminds me of goodness. And you're also the 'Beats' in my heart, who always makes my life more rhythmic and full of spirit.”
